chunk_findings.detail:
The marker filter is cleared for the whole pytest invocation, not just the named test. The guard is `any("::" in t for t in py_tests)`, which by construction allows a mixed selection list — and the `run_command(cmd, py_tests, root)` signature is the generic selector used by the affected-tests/regression-test gate, so `py_tests` is not restricted to bare node ids. Input: `py_tests = ["tests/test_slow.py", "tests/test_scenarios.py::test_crash_recovery"]` with a project `pytest.ini` containing `addopts = -m 'not slow'`. The returned command becomes
`python -m pytest -q -m '' tests/test_slow.py tests/test_scenarios.py::test_crash_recovery`,
so every `@pytest.mark.slow` test in `tests/test_slow.py` is now collected and executed, although the project deliberately deselects those in `addopts` (and the other selection path — file-level entries, no `::` — previously kept that filter intact). For a change that only asked to run one named test via `--regression-test`, the gate now runs the whole slow set: if those slow tests need network/live services, hang, or exceed the gate's time budget, `ddflow complete`/the affected-tests gate fails (exit 2/1) or stalls for an unrelated reason. Only the named node id needed the filter lifted; clearing `-m` for every test in the same invocation is the over-reach. A scoped alternative is to run the named node id in its own invocation (or only clear `-m` when `py_tests` is exactly the named id), keeping the project's marker economy on the rest of the selection.

chunk_findings.detail:
The guard is `any("::" in t for t in py_tests)` but the option it appends (`-m ""`) is a *process‑global* override, and `py_tests` is a list (the author's use of `any` over the list implies several entries are expected in one invocation). Whenever the selection mixes a named nodeid with whole‑file entries — exactly what `ddflow complete … --regression-test <nodeid>` does if the affected‑tests closure (file paths) is run together with the appended regression nodeid — the suite's marker filter is disabled for *every* item, not just the named one.

Concrete input: `run_command(f"{sys.executable} -m pytest -q", ["tests/test_net_and_slow.py", "tests/test_a.py::test_quick"], root)` on a project whose `pytest.ini` has `addopts = -m 'not slow and not network'`. Before the change the command was `… -m 'not slow and not network' tests/test_net_and_slow.py tests/test_a.py::test_quick`; after the change it is `… -m '' tests/test_net_and_slow.py tests/test_a.py::test_quick` (because the second element contains `::`), so the previously deselected `slow`/`network` tests in `tests/test_net_and_slow.py` are collected and executed — long‑running or network‑touching tests now fire on a routine `complete`, and any explicit `-m` filter supplied by the user/base command is silently clobbered as well. The fix only needs to keep the *named* test from being deselected; an empty global `-m` also removes every other marker exclusion for the co‑selected files.

chunk_findings.detail: The condition only clears the marker filter when *every* entry is a node id. For a mixed selection that the author's own new test declares reachable (`["a.py", "b.py::test_x"]`), `all(...)` is False, so `"not slow"` from `addopts` stays in effect and a *named slow* test is still deselected — the exact failure mode of Bc332daa185. Concretely: `run_command("pytest -q", ["tests/test_other.py", "tests/test_scenarios.py::test_crash_recovery_..."], root)` with `addopts = -m 'not slow'` and that node id marked `slow` emits no `-m ""`; pytest then runs the tests collected from `tests/test_other.py`, reports the named test as deselected, and exits 0. The gate therefore records a successful regression run in which the named slow test never executed, so the bug can be closed without the regression test passing — a silent false success that is worse than the old exit-5 "no tests ran". This is a regression relative to the previous `any(...)` code, which at least ran the named test in this input (its over-inclusive running of slow tests in the whole file is what the earlier finding flagged, but the new code fixes over-inclusion by reintroducing under-selection for the named node id in the same list). A correct fix has to treat the two kinds of selector differently (e.g. two invocations, or `-m ""` scoped to the named node ids rather than the whole invocation).

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard `all("::" in t for t in py_tests)` only lifts the suite's marker filter when *every* target is a nodeid. The comment it guards states the invariant "A NAMED test is asked for by id: the suite's marker filter (`-m 'not slow'` in addopts) must not deselect it" — but `all` violates that invariant as soon as one whole-file target is present. Given `run_command("pytest -q", ["tests/test_other.py", "tests/test_scenarios.py::test_crash_recovery_does_not_race_the_clock_for_its_live_window_checks"], root)` where the named test is `@pytest.mark.slow`, `all(...)` is `False`, so `["-m", ""]` is not appended and pytest's default `-m 'not slow'` deselects the named test → exit 5, "no tests ran" — the exact failure Bc332daa185 is meant to fix. The author's own new test `test_a_file_among_the_selection_keeps_the_marker_filter` (`["a.py", "b.py::test_x"]` → asserts `"-m" not in got.split()`) codifies precisely this case, i.e. it locks in the deselection of the named test whenever a file is part of the selection. The fix therefore only works when the regression nodeid is the sole argument; if `complete --regression-test` runs the nodeid together with the affected-tests file closure in one invocation (the scenario the previous report described), the bug is not fixed at all and no test in the diff catches it (the existing regression test passes only `["test_s.py::test_slow"]`).

chunk_findings.detail: When a `ci run --full` succeeds, this records a `cadence.ran / integration_tests` pass whose only account of what was tested is the free-text note `f"ci run --full on {ref}"`. The phase-close gate that reads this record can key on event kind, cadence name and timestamp, but not on the tree that actually passed. Concretely, an operator runs `ddflow ci run --full` on an unmerged branch, a different phase's worktree, or a dirty working tree after the phase's last merge; the record is newer than the merge and certifies `schedule.phase_full_suite`, so the phase closes even though the phase's merged tree never had the full suite run. That contradicts the stated intent ("a recorded pass … on the phase's merged tree"). A structured field carrying the merge commit/tree identity (and the gate verifying it against the phase's merge) is needed; a note is not machine-checkable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/cirun.py:113-115

chunk_findings.detail: The gate is keyed on the completed item's kind being `"phase"`, but the stated rule is that a phase must not close when "a phase's last task completes, or its acceptance task is completed", and specifically that "`complete` of a phase acceptance task refuses without it". An acceptance task (and the last ordinary task of a phase) is an item of kind `task`/`acceptance`, not `phase`, so for `ddflow complete <phase-acceptance-task>` the condition at complete.py:116 is `False`, `_phase_suite` is never invoked, and the phase closes with no full-suite record — exactly the case the intent says must be refused. The `closing` branch immediately below ("The one blocker the flag is about to clear") is where the phase actually gets closed on that path, which is why the check belongs there (`if closing and ...`) rather than on `it.kind == "phase"`; as written, only an explicit completion of the `phase` item is gated, and a phase whose tasks passed on selected scope can still be closed via its acceptance task. Demonstrated input: with `[schedule].phase_full_suite = "require"`, no `integration_tests` cadence newer than the phase's last merge, and the phase's acceptance task complete-able, running `ddflow complete <acceptance-task>` appends no blocker and the phase closes — the scenario the test ("a phase whose tasks pass on selected scope cannot close until the full-suite record exists") is supposed to reject.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py:116 (`if it.kind == "phase" and cfg.schedule.phase_full_suite != "off":`)

chunk_findings.detail: `missing` opens the gate on a non-strict comparison: `if not merged or passed >= merged:`. The intent (and the function's own docstring, line 26: "when a full-suite pass *newer* than the phase's last merge exists") requires the pass to be strictly newer than the last merge. With `>=`, a pass whose timestamp equals the last merge is accepted as valid. This is reachable whenever timestamps share granularity (e.g. ISO strings truncated to the second, which is common for `ts`/`at` fields): a task merges at `2026-10-16T10:00:00Z` and an `integration_tests` pass recorded at `2026-10-16T10:00:00Z` on the *pre*-merge tree (same second, recorded immediately before the merge) makes `passed >= merged` true, so `missing` returns `""` and the acceptance task can complete even though the merged tree was never run against the full suite. The comparison should be `passed > merged` so equality does not count as "newer".
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/phase_suite.py:28

chunk_findings.detail:
The transcript has been rewritten so that every `ddflow upgrade` invocation now expects the same fatal error:

    ManifestError: unreleased fragment knob_added.schedule.phase_full_suite.toml change #1: impact 'behavior' is not one of additive, deprecating, breaking

and correspondingly `upgrade` (exit 1), `upgrade --plan` (exit 1), `upgrade --apply` (previously exit 3 with a confirmation prompt, now exit 1 with empty stdout), `upgrade --apply hooks` (previously exit 0 "Up to date: nothing to apply.", now exit 1, changed in this diff) and even the unrelated `upgrade --category nosuch` case (its "unknown upgrade category" message is entirely replaced) all now fail at manifest-load time. This is not a behavior of the surface being tested — it is the new feature's own unreleased manifest fragment `knob_added.schedule.phase_full_suite.toml` declaring `impact = "behavior"`, a value the manifest validator rejects (allowed: additive, deprecating, breaking). Instead of correcting the fragment's `impact` (e.g. to `additive`), the diff only records the failure into the golden transcript, so the tests pass while the whole `upgrade` command — including `--apply` and per-category application — is dead. Given input `ddflow upgrade --apply hooks`, the surface now exits 1 with an empty stdout instead of applying nothing and reporting "Up to date", which is a regression in the upgrade surface caused by the new fragment, and the transcript change is what hides it. The fragment must be fixed and these expectations restored; recording the ManifestError as the expected output is the defect.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json (upgrade scenario, all changed expectations)

chunk_findings.detail: The transcript now records that `ddflow upgrade` aborts with `ManifestError: unreleased fragment knob_added.schedule.phase_full_suite.toml change #1: impact 'behavior' is not one of additive, deprecating, breaking` and emits an empty stdout, where it previously emitted the full upgrade plan ("ddflow <VERSION>; ... 1 upgrade item(s) pending ... data repairs (1) ..."). This is not a benign expectation update: the new manifest fragment `knob_added.schedule.phase_full_suite.toml` declares `impact = "behavior"`, which the manifest validator rejects because impact must be one of `additive`, `deprecating`, `breaking`. Any command that loads the manifest (here the recorded setup-ops runs with args `k`/`r`/`bogus`) now fails before doing any work, so the whole `phase_full_suite` feature is unreachable via the manifest path, and the test has been "fixed" by baking the failure into the expected transcript (stdout `""` + stderr error) instead of correcting the fragment's impact value. Demonstrate by running `ddflow upgrade` on a tree containing that fragment: it returns the ManifestError above and prints nothing, rather than the pending-upgrade plan the old transcript asserted.

chunk_findings.detail: The new knob's explain text justifies the check with decision id `D-gate-economy-r3`, but every other place this project states the same fact uses `D-test-economy-r2` — the change's own intent names `D-test-economy-r2`, and this same transcript, in `cadence.integration_tests_every_tasks`, writes "An item's ci and unit_tests gates run only the tests its change reaches (D-test-economy-r2)". The gate-economy family is also spelled elsewhere in this file without an `-r` suffix and with a space: "decision D-gate-economy 1", "D-gate-economy 2", "D-gate-economy 3" (`gates.unit_tests_scope`, `review.max_rounds`, `review.delta_default`), so `D-gate-economy-r3` is not a form that family uses. This file is the golden fixture for `tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.py` (also pinned in `ci.always_tests`), which compares this text byte-for-byte against `config --explain` output; if the source description carries the correct `D-test-economy-r2`, this fixture no longer matches and the transcript test fails, and if the source has been changed to match the fixture, the wrong decision id is what every operator and agent now reads from the explain output for a knob whose whole point is auditable phase-close evidence.

chunk_findings.detail: The gate is keyed on the *completed item's kind* being `"phase"`, but the intent this change implements gates the completion of the phase's **tasks**, not just the phase item: "When a phase's last task completes, or its acceptance task is completed, the FULL suite must have passed … `complete` of a phase acceptance task refuses without it", with the stated test being "a phase whose tasks pass on selected scope cannot close until the full-suite record exists". Those completions are items whose `kind` is `"task"` and whose enclosing phase is already computed and passed into the very next call as `umbrella` / detected by the existing `closing` flag (`hard = _failed_review(repo, cfg, st, item, v, umbrella); if closing: …`). Concretely: run `ddflow complete <phase-acceptance-task-id>` (a task, `it.kind == "task"`, `closing` true) on a phase whose tasks only passed on selected scope — this `if` is false, `_phase_suite` is never called, no blocker is appended, and the phase closes without any `integration_tests` pass/record, which is exactly the scenario the feature's test is meant to refuse. The condition should be the phase-closing signal (`closing` / `umbrella`), not `it.kind == "phase"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py:116 (`if it.kind == "phase" and cfg.schedule.phase_full_suite != "off":`)

chunk_findings.detail: `missing()` accepts a full-suite pass that is not actually newer than the phase's last merge: the guard returns "" (gate open) whenever `passed >= merged`, but both the module docstring ("It counts when it is NEWER than the last merge") and the intent ("requires a recorded pass newer than the last merge") demand a strictly newer pass. Concrete case: a `worktree.merged` event for the phase's last task stamped `2026-10-16T12:00:00.900000Z`, and the `integration_tests` cadence record stamped `2026-10-16T12:00:00.100000Z` (i.e. the suite finished 800 ms *before* the merge). With sub-second truncation (or any coarse/replayed stamping), both collapse to the same value, or the pass is simply older-yet-equal after truncation, and `passed >= merged` is true, so `missing()` returns "" and the phase acceptance task is allowed to complete even though no suite run ever saw the merged tree. Changing the operator to `>` (and comparing parsed timestamps rather than raw strings, since a lexicographic comparison of ISO strings with differing fractional-second/timezone precision, e.g. `...T12:00:00Z` vs `...T12:00:00.500000Z`, also orders an earlier pass above a later merge) is required to match the stated gate.

chunk_findings.detail: This part of the change deletes the user-facing line `Upgraded ddflow to <VERSION> (this project predates version stamps): run \`ddflow upgrade --plan\`` from three recorded golden outputs, while the stated intent (and the rest of this diff) is only about phase closing / `schedule.phase_full_suite`. Nothing in the intent says the "predates version stamps" upgrade nudge should stop being emitted, yet the three snapshots are what `tests/golden/test_golden_outputs.py` compares against. Demonstrate: run the golden case for a project without a version stamp (the tuples at old lines 220/276/333) — the CLI still takes the "predates version stamps" path and prints the upgrade line, so the stored snapshot no longer matches and all three golden assertions fail; if instead the emitter was changed to stop printing it, then a long-standing operator-facing upgrade prompt has been silently removed and the intent gives no rationale, i.e. an undocumented behaviour change riding along in a snapshot update. Either way the deletion is not justified by the change being reviewed and needs to be separated out or explained.

chunk_findings.detail: The new expected stderr is `ManifestError: unreleased fragment knob_added.schedule.phase_full_suite.toml change #1: impact 'behavior' is not one of additive, deprecating, breaking`. The changelog fragment added by this change sets `impact = "behavior"`, but the manifest validator accepts only `additive`, `deprecating`, `breaking`. The consequence is not scoped to this test: in any project that carries the fragment, `ddflow upgrade` refuses at fragment-validation time before doing any work. The transcript itself demonstrates the blast radius — the plain `upgrade` plan that previously emitted the unknown-author repair plan now emits empty stdout plus this error; `upgrade --apply` moves from exit 3 / `[refused] repair:unknown-author-shards ...` to exit 1 with no output; `upgrade --apply hooks` moves from exit 0 / `Up to date: nothing to apply.` to exit 1. Concretely: run `ddflow upgrade --plan` in a repo containing `.ddflow` with this fragment and you get exit 1 and no plan, where before you got the plan and exit 0. The fragment must be authored with a valid impact value (e.g. `additive`), not by baking the validation failure into the transcripts.

chunk_findings.detail: The change rewrites the golden expectation for `ddflow upgrade` so that stdout is now empty and stderr is `ManifestError: unreleased fragment knob_added.schedule.phase_full_suite.toml change #1: impact 'behavior' is not one of additive, deprecating, breaking`. That message is not an intended output — `'behavior'` is an invalid impact value; the manifest schema accepts only `additive`, `deprecating`, `breaking`. Given any project whose tree contains the new unreleased fragment `knob_added.schedule.phase_full_suite.toml`, `ddflow upgrade` (even in plan-only mode, as the previously-recorded output "plan only; nothing was written" shows) aborts before producing the plan, emits the plan text nowhere, and exits with a manifest error. The correct remediation is to set `impact = "additive"` (or `deprecating`/`breaking`) in the fragment; instead the transcript was edited to codify the broken output as expected, so the three affected cases now assert that the upgrade command produces no plan and an error, permanently masking the regression and leaving the phase_full_suite knob unusable via `upgrade`. chunk_findings.detail: The gate is keyed on the *completed item's kind* being `"phase"`, but the intent this change implements gates the completion of the phase's **tasks**, not just the phase item: "When a phase's last task completes, or its acceptance task is completed, the FULL suite must have passed … `complete` of a phase acceptance task refuses without it", with the stated test being "a phase whose tasks pass on selected scope cannot close until the full-suite record exists". Those completions are items whose `kind` is `"task"` and whose enclosing phase is already computed and passed into the very next call as `umbrella` / detected by the existing `closing` flag (`hard = _failed_review(repo, cfg, st, item, v, umbrella); if closing: …`). Concretely: run `ddflow complete <phase-acceptance-task-id>` (a task, `it.kind == "task"`, `closing` true) on a phase whose tasks only passed on selected scope — this `if` is false, `_phase_suite` is never called, no blocker is appended, and the phase closes without any `integration_tests` pass/record, which is exactly the scenario the feature's test is meant to refuse. The condition should be the phase-closing signal (`closing` / `umbrella`), not `it.kind == "phase"`.

chunk_findings.detail: `missing()` accepts a full-suite pass that is not actually newer than the phase's last merge: the guard returns "" (gate open) whenever `passed >= merged`, but both the module docstring ("It counts when it is NEWER than the last merge") and the intent ("requires a recorded pass newer than the last merge") demand a strictly newer pass. Concrete case: a `worktree.merged` event for the phase's last task stamped `2026-10-16T12:00:00.900000Z`, and the `integration_tests` cadence record stamped `2026-10-16T12:00:00.100000Z` (i.e. the suite finished 800 ms *before* the merge). With sub-second truncation (or any coarse/replayed stamping), both collapse to the same value, or the pass is simply older-yet-equal after truncation, and `passed >= merged` is true, so `missing()` returns "" and the phase acceptance task is allowed to complete even though no suite run ever saw the merged tree. Changing the operator to `>` (and comparing parsed timestamps rather than raw strings, since a lexicographic comparison of ISO strings with differing fractional-second/timezone precision, e.g. `...T12:00:00Z` vs `...T12:00:00.500000Z`, also orders an earlier pass above a later merge) is required to match the stated gate.

The changelog fragment added by this change sets `impact = "behavior"`, but the manifest validator accepts only `additive`, `deprecating`, `breaking`. The consequence is not scoped to this test: in any project that carries the fragment, `ddflow upgrade` refuses at fragment-validation time before doing any work. The transcript itself demonstrates the blast radius — the plain `upgrade` plan that previously emitted the unknown-author repair plan now emits empty stdout plus this error; `upgrade --apply` moves from exit 3 / `[refused] repair:unknown-author-shards ...` to exit 1 with no output; `upgrade --apply hooks` moves from exit 0 / `Up to date: nothing to apply.` to exit 1. chunk_findings.detail: When a `ci run --full` succeeds, this records a `cadence.ran / integration_tests` pass whose only account of what was tested is the free-text note `f"ci run --full on {ref}"`. The phase-close gate that reads this record can key on event kind, cadence name and timestamp, but not on the tree that actually passed. Concretely, an operator runs `ddflow ci run --full` on an unmerged branch, a different phase's worktree, or a dirty working tree after the phase's last merge; the record is newer than the merge and certifies `schedule.phase_full_suite`, so the phase closes even though the phase's merged tree never had the full suite run. That contradicts the stated intent ("a recorded pass … on the phase's merged tree"). A structured field carrying the merge commit/tree identity (and the gate verifying it against the phase's merge) is needed; a note is not machine-checkable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/cirun.py:113-115

chunk_findings.detail: The gate is keyed on the completed item's kind being `"phase"`, but the stated rule is that a phase must not close when "a phase's last task completes, or its acceptance task is completed", and specifically that "`complete` of a phase acceptance task refuses without it". An acceptance task (and the last ordinary task of a phase) is an item of kind `task`/`acceptance`, not `phase`, so for `ddflow complete <phase-acceptance-task>` the condition at complete.py:116 is `False`, `_phase_suite` is never invoked, and the phase closes with no full-suite record — exactly the case the intent says must be refused. The `closing` branch immediately below ("The one blocker the flag is about to clear") is where the phase actually gets closed on that path, which is why the check belongs there (`if closing and ...`) rather than on `it.kind == "phase"`; as written, only an explicit completion of the `phase` item is gated, and a phase whose tasks passed on selected scope can still be closed via its acceptance task. Demonstrated input: with `[schedule].phase_full_suite = "require"`, no `integration_tests` cadence newer than the phase's last merge, and the phase's acceptance task complete-able, running `ddflow complete <acceptance-task>` appends no blocker and the phase closes — the scenario the test ("a phase whose tasks pass on selected scope cannot close until the full-suite record exists") is supposed to reject.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py:116 (`if it.kind == "phase" and cfg.schedule.phase_full_suite != "off":`)

chunk_findings.detail: `missing` opens the gate on a non-strict comparison: `if not merged or passed >= merged:`. The intent (and the function's own docstring, line 26: "when a full-suite pass *newer* than the phase's last merge exists") requires the pass to be strictly newer than the last merge. With `>=`, a pass whose timestamp equals the last merge is accepted as valid. This is reachable whenever timestamps share granularity (e.g. ISO strings truncated to the second, which is common for `ts`/`at` fields): a task merges at `2026-10-16T10:00:00Z` and an `integration_tests` pass recorded at `2026-10-16T10:00:00Z` on the *pre*-merge tree (same second, recorded immediately before the merge) makes `passed >= merged` true, so `missing` returns `""` and the acceptance task can complete even though the merged tree was never run against the full suite. The comparison should be `passed > merged` so equality does not count as "newer".

chunk_findings.detail:
The transcript has been rewritten so that every `ddflow upgrade` invocation now expects the same fatal error:

    ManifestError: unreleased fragment knob_added.schedule.phase_full_suite.toml change #1: impact 'behavior' is not one of additive, deprecating, breaking

and correspondingly `upgrade` (exit 1), `upgrade --plan` (exit 1), `upgrade --apply` (previously exit 3 with a confirmation prompt, now exit 1 with empty stdout), `upgrade --apply hooks` (previously exit 0 "Up to date: nothing to apply.", now exit 1, changed in this diff) and even the unrelated `upgrade --category nosuch` case (its "unknown upgrade category" message is entirely replaced) all now fail at manifest-load time. This is not a behavior of the surface being tested — it is the new feature's own unreleased manifest fragment `knob_added.schedule.phase_full_suite.toml` declaring `impact = "behavior"`, a value the manifest validator rejects (allowed: additive, deprecating, breaking). Instead of correcting the fragment's `impact` (e.g. to `additive`), the diff only records the failure into the golden transcript, so the tests pass while the whole `upgrade` command — including `--apply` and per-category application — is dead. Given input `ddflow upgrade --apply hooks`, the surface now exits 1 with an empty stdout instead of applying nothing and reporting "Up to date", which is a regression in the upgrade surface caused by the new fragment, and the transcript change is what hides it. The fragment must be fixed and these expectations restored; recording the ManifestError as the expected output is the defect.

The fix only swapped the stdout/stderr strings and left the `1,` exit-code line and the three distinct argument tails untouched, so it re-creates in the opposite direction exactly the defect the previous review reported (every upgrade invocation pinned to one output). Either the `bogus` entry must expect an argument-error on stderr (non-zero), or the fix copied one recorded plan across entries that are not the same invocation.
